text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ontario riot report finds most at fault: Protesters, politicians and police all under fire in review of demonstration.
- Former Saskatchewan premier Grant Devine knew of plan to set up secret bank account, trial told.
- Zaire steps closer to disaster: Refugees flee as fighting intensifies.
- Few Canadians succumbing to Internet's allure.
- Canadian government lifts federal sales tax on books for select group of buyers: Schools, libraries, charities benefit from industry lobbying.
- Fresh evidence found of mad-cow link.
- False Canadian address used to buy shares for Fidelity Investments mutual fund manager.
- Canadian mortgage rates slide again: Five-year loan of 7.2 percent is lowest long-term rate since 1967.
- Rogers Communications Inc. eyes selling Cantel stake to AT&T Canada: Deal could be worth C$600 million.
- Quebec moves to deregulate electricity market: U.S. customers will benefit from move to open government-owned power grid.
- Cost-cutting pushes Canada's two major railways toward profitability.
- Canadian retailers shocked by move to blend sales taxes in Atlantic Canada.
- Bre-X Minerals Ltd. lawyers met with Indonesian partners to settle claim.
